estimand.description: Average gap between Iran's annual CPI inflation (percentage points) and a synthetic Iran without the 2012 sanctions tightening, 2012-2015

design.title: 2012 sanctions tightening and inflation in Iran
design.research_question: How much did the 2012 tightening of international sanctions on Iran (EU oil embargo, central-bank sanctions) change Iran's annual CPI inflation in 2012-2015?
design.assignment_mechanism: policy shock imposed on one country in 2012; comparison countries never treated
design.interference_assessment: spillovers to trade partners possible but assumed second order for donor inflation
design.missingness_plan: donors restricted to complete 1996-2015 series; exclusions listed in the report
design.sensitivity_plan: in-space and in-time placebo tests; donor pool rule declared in prepare_panel.py
design.primary_analysis: synthetic control on annual CPI inflation

assumption_justifications.parallel_trends: Synthetic-control analogue: absent the 2012 tightening, Iran's inflation would have followed the weighted donor combination that reproduces 1996-2011.
assumption_justifications.no_anticipation: Sanctions were tightened at the end of 2011 and in 2012; earlier anticipation effects would bias the estimate toward zero and are checked with an in-time placebo.
assumption_justifications.stable_composition: Same countries and the same World Bank CPI definition throughout.
assumption_justifications.timing_handled: A single treated unit with a single start date; no staggered adoption.
